item.title: Who deserves to know I am HIV positive?
item.description: “It is due to the stigma that my parents and siblings remain unaware of my HIV history. It’s been three years since the diagnosis, one year since I reached undetectable.”

item.title: Uganda’s first peace journalism awards redefine the media landscape
item.description: The PJF’s framework seeks to move the media beyond sensationalism toward peace and development-oriented reporting, emphasizing early identification of conflict triggers and the promotion of non-violent responses.

item.title: The upcoming election will determine the future of Bangladesh’s democracy and reform agenda
item.description: Three contradictions threaten Bangladesh’s democratic transition: flawed referendum mechanics, exclusionary digital campaigns, and systematic gender marginalisation, revealing elite male circulation.

item.title: Why Japan’s upcoming lower house election feels like a race to the bottom
item.description: As an ethnic Chinese, born and raised in Japan, I see the virtues of reticence and reserve being weaponized to hollow out our democracy, in particular during troubled times.

item.title: Researchers in Africa are using AI to fill the global health care gap
item.description: Africa has 11 percent of the world’s population and 24 percent of the global disease burden, yet only 3 percent of the world’s health workers and less than 1 percent of global health expenditure.

item.title: Life as a migrant ‘host’ in the red-light district of Chiang Mai, Thailand
item.description: “Living in Thailand, if you don’t have money, you can’t go anywhere. It’s like migrants need to have money all the time.”

item.title: Malaysian journalist briefly detained for sedition over a question during a public lecture
item.description: "Can a journalist be deemed to have committed sedition or caused public mischief simply by asking a question at a public forum?

item.title: The social media battlefield: Political campaigns in Bangladesh’s national elections
item.description: Bangladeshi political parties compete for Gen Z’s attention with viral content, while battling misinformation alongside street campaigning, as Facebook, TikTok, and YouTube become central arenas for political messaging and debate.

item.title: Hong Kong media tycoon Jimmy Lai receives a 20-year jail sentence
item.description: Jimmy Lai's sentence marks the harshest punishment among all prosecutions under the 2020 National Security Law, enacted by Beijing in Hong Kong.

item.title: Women and young girls bear the brunt of Mali’s worsening security crisis
item.description: Since 2012, Mali has been in security turmoil with the emergence and expansion of several radical non-State armed groups. This situation disproportionately affects the civilian population, especially women and girls.
